home.heroSubtitle: Sign in once with Keycloak, grant only the data scopes each department actually needs, and track every application from a single, unified view — instead of a separate login and a separate form for every department.
home.featuresTitle: Built as a real interoperability layer
home.featureKeycloakDescription: Every login and every API call is verified against Keycloak — the single identity authority for citizens, officers, and platform administrators alike.
home.featureConsentDescription: At registration you choose exactly which categories of your data OneDesk may hold — name and photo by default, everything else opt-in and revocable in Settings at any time.
home.featureConnectorsDescription: Identity, Business Registry, Revenue, Municipal Corporation, and License Authority are wired up as real connectors — OAuth, SOAP, REST, a direct database link, and GraphQL.
home.featureTrackingTitle: One application, tracked end to end
home.featureTrackingDescription: Submit once and watch the same application move through every department it touches, with real-time status updates as each step completes.
home.footerTagline: A unified interoperability platform connecting citizens with every government department.
home.footerAccessibilityDescription: Skip-to-content, keyboard-navigable menus, and adjustable text size are available on every page.

help.title: Help & Support
help.subtitle: Answers to common questions, and ways to reach us.
help.faq1Question: Why do I only need to enter my information once?
help.faq1Answer: OneDesk securely fetches verified data you have already provided to one department — like your income certificate or academic records — when another department needs it, with your consent.
help.faq2Question: Can a department access my data without my permission?
help.faq2Answer: No. Every cross-department data request requires your explicit, purpose-bound consent, which you can review and revoke anytime from My Consents.
help.faq3Question: How do I track an application that involves multiple departments?
help.faq3Answer: Open My Applications and select the application. The timeline shows every step across every department involved, in one place.
help.faq4Question: What happens if a department system is temporarily unavailable?
help.faq4Answer: Your application continues to progress on any steps that do not depend on that department. You will be notified once the affected step resumes.

architectureTab.intro: The actual deployment topology, left → right. Every node is a separate container; every line is a real network call in the codebase, not an illustration.
architectureTab.hoverHint: Hover or click a node to follow its real connections — everything else fades.
architectureTab.selectNodePrompt: Select a node to see its real connections and role.
architectureTab.whyGatewayDescription: Kong is the single entry point for every request from the browser — it routes <code1>/api/*</code1> to core-api and <code2>/mdm/*</code2> to mdm-service, and handles CORS and rate-limiting centrally. The frontend never talks to a backend container directly. Adapters are called by core-api directly — Kong never proxies them.
architectureTab.whyTwoDatabasesDescription: Municipal Corporation's adapter writes to its own Postgres database, separate from core-api's — genuinely independent storage, not a shared "central database." Every other adapter is stateless; this one is real database-backed, matching its DB protocol label.
